prompt:
You are the Failure-Lens Proposer. From only the general task seed and the fixed goal of producing an implementable requirements handoff, propose 3-5 distinct externally observable ways discovery, interaction, synthesis, handoff, implementation, verification, or learning can fail. Do not propose solutions or skill wording and do not name or compare products, agents, skills, or frameworks.
Return only the JSON object required by the supplied output schema.
INPUT:
{"fixed_goal":"surface material ambiguity and produce an implementable requirements handoff","seed_category":"Preserve all existing behavior while adding an optional --json flag to the todo list command so automation can consume task records."}

input.seed_category: Preserve all existing behavior while adding an optional --json flag to the todo list command so automation can consume task records.
input.fixed_goal: surface material ambiguity and produce an implementable requirements handoff

lenses.failure_description: Existing human-readable behavior or undocumented output conventions are missed, so the change alters default command behavior despite the preservation requirement.
lenses.observable_signal: Running the command without --json produces different text, ordering, spacing, exit status, or side effects than before.
lenses.why_material: The explicit compatibility requirement is violated and existing users or scripts may break.
lenses.minimal_test_shape: Capture representative pre-change default invocations, then compare their stdout, stderr, exit status, ordering, and side effects against the changed command without --json.

lenses.failure_description: Material questions about which task fields, value types, nullability, identifiers, and ordering belong in each JSON record remain unresolved.
lenses.observable_signal: Different implementers produce incompatible JSON shapes from the same task data, or consumers must guess how to interpret missing and optional values.
lenses.why_material: Automation cannot reliably parse or depend on an unspecified data contract.
lenses.minimal_test_shape: Present records containing complete, missing, optional, and unusual field values and check whether one unambiguous expected JSON representation can be stated for each.

lenses.failure_description: The handoff does not clearly distinguish JSON payload output from diagnostics, warnings, progress text, or empty-result behavior.
lenses.observable_signal: A successful --json invocation emits non-JSON text on stdout, or empty and error cases cannot be parsed consistently.
lenses.why_material: Any extra or undefined stdout content can make the command unusable in automated pipelines.
lenses.minimal_test_shape: Exercise successful, empty, warning-producing, and failing invocations with --json and verify whether stdout is consistently parseable according to a single stated contract.

lenses.failure_description: The --json path applies different filtering, sorting, selection, or task retrieval semantics from the existing list command.
lenses.observable_signal: For identical arguments and underlying tasks, the JSON result represents a different record set or order than the default listing.
lenses.why_material: The flag would change command meaning rather than only provide an automation-consumable representation.
lenses.minimal_test_shape: Run matched default and --json invocations across filters, sort options, empty data, and multiple tasks, then compare represented task identities and ordering.

lenses.failure_description: Verification demonstrates valid JSON in a happy path but does not establish preservation of existing behavior or correctness across edge and failure cases.
lenses.observable_signal: Tests pass while regressions remain in default output, option combinations, special characters, empty lists, or error exit statuses.
lenses.why_material: The handoff can appear complete without proving either half of the goal: compatibility and dependable machine consumption.
lenses.minimal_test_shape: Use a compact matrix covering flag absent versus present, zero versus multiple records, escaped text, option combinations, and command failures; assert output channel, parseability, record equivalence, and exit status.
